weak.title: Weak scaling, blast lattice, subcycled: s per coarse step
weak.note: Same physics, grid and dt. MFC: integrated build (5d8ab069, owner placement on), single case-optimized build, 2 reps. Efficiency 8->512 GPUs: MFC 0.85, AMReX 0.69, PeleC 0.63. At 512 GPUs MFC is faster per step than PeleC (0.90 vs 0.95 s). MFC refines more volume (40.5% vs 30.3%). 1024-GPU rung queued.

conv.title: MFC: subcycled minus lock-step solution vs level-0 dt
conv.note: Plotted: max difference between subcycled and lock-step solutions (not error vs exact). Conservation: subcycled runs within 1.5e-15, lock-step two-level runs within 7.9e-15 (roundoff); 1 and 4 ranks bit-identical. Quartic prolongation (amr_prolong = 2) makes subcycling second order; with regrid, new fine cells must also be seeded with the quartic (fix found by diffing against the mini-app).

cov.title: Refined share of the domain at matched time
cov.note: Coverage of the grid actually used in the last timed steps (regrid after step 220). MFC required same-level blocks to meet face to face, so each blast became one bounding cube; the new opt-in tile clustering brings MFC to AMReX's refined volume (15.3% vs 15.45%, 29.6% vs 30.25%), currently 4x slower per step until its per-block work is batched.

phase.title: Where MFC's time goes, blast L, 8 GPUs (before the fixes)
phase.note: Fill and halo = gather + gfill + halo + seam. Other = swap + rk. Level-0 RHS alone is 80 ms per stage for 8M cells per GPU; the mini-app's whole non-subcycled step is 95 ms.

convm.title: Mini-app: the same test, minmod vs quartic
convm.note: The C/HIP reference implementation found the prolongation limit first (finding F1) and predicted the quartic fix that MFC now confirms.

amr.title: AMR-only cost per coarse step (everything except each code's own hydro RHS)
amr.note: Integrated MFC build. MFC's AMR-only cost is below AMReX's in both modes and below PeleC's from 64 GPUs on (0.31 vs 0.48 s at 512 subcycled; 0.08 vs 0.18 s lock-step vs AMReX).

status.title: Ready to show
items: Flagship movie: Mach 2.5 shock through a curtain of 64 free spheres, 80 GPUs, volumetric shocks, vortex wakes, GPU-coloured cutaway with callouts, plus three 4K hero stills: curtain movie and stills. Second example: 8-sphere movie.

Subcycling in MFC: one and two refined levels, conservative to ~1e-15, bit-identical across ranks, second order with quartic prolongation (also with regrid). Quartic interfaces match a uniform fine grid; minmod is 10^4-10^5x worse (figure below). Full GPU regression suite 789/789.

Weak scaling vs PeleC and AMReX: newest MFC build at 128 GPUs is 0.716 s/step subcycled vs PeleC 0.832 and AMReX 0.613, efficiency 0.94 vs 0.72/0.76, time to solution 149 s vs PeleC 172 s. Previous build to 512 GPUs: efficiency 0.85 vs AMReX 0.69, PeleC 0.63, and faster than PeleC per step (0.90 vs 0.95 s).
AMR-only cost (each code's own RHS excluded): newest MFC 0.155 s/step subcycled at 128 GPUs vs AMReX 0.421 and PeleC 0.358; lock-step 0.048 vs AMReX 0.149.
Reference mini-app: 2.6-4.5x faster per step than AMReX/PeleC at 512 GPUs, 0.95-0.96 weak-scaling efficiency with owner placement; its findings drove the MFC fixes.

Found and fixed, with evidence: reflux race (multi-rank nondeterminism), snap crash, first-order subcycling from minmod seeding, regrid out-of-memory at 128 GPUs, coverage matched to AMReX with tile clustering.

status.title: Newest: subcycling driver + swap packing
items: Pushed to spike/amr-integrate (7273d602); bitwise identical to the previous build, AMR tests pass.
Subcycled s/step 0.762 -> 0.674 (np8), 0.787 -> 0.699 (np64), about 12% faster; AMR-only time down ~40% (0.231 -> 0.141 s at np64). Lock-step 0.251 -> 0.231 (np8).
At 128 GPUs (2 reps): subcycled 0.833 -> 0.716 s/step, lock-step 0.263 -> 0.243. The 512- and 1024-GPU runs of this build start ~05:12-06:12 tomorrow, alongside the 1024-GPU rung for AMReX and PeleC.

Tile clustering: not ready. Subcycled runs exhaust GPU memory at the step-140 regrid (store slots are sized for full 64^3 blocks); lock-step is 2-2.7x slower with no coverage gain. Fix = per-block slot sizing, post-meeting.

figs.caption: 4K hero still: vortex rings among shocked spheres in the particle curtain (80 GPUs).

MFC vs AMReX CNS vs PeleC, subcycled. Newest MFC build (subcycling driver + swap packing, 7273d602) at 8-128 GPUs: efficiency 0.94 at 128 (AMReX 0.76, PeleC 0.72), 0.716 s/step vs PeleC 0.832 and AMReX 0.613. Light line: previous build to 512 GPUs (efficiency 0.85 vs 0.69/0.63). Newest build at 512/1024 GPUs runs overnight.
Sponsor version: MFC vs PeleC, subcycled. MFC is faster per step from 64 GPUs on (0.716 vs 0.832 s at 128), adds a tenth of PeleC's AMR cost with scale, and holds 0.94 efficiency at 128 GPUs vs 0.72.

What each fix bought, MFC subcycled at 64 GPUs: 1.95 -> 0.70 s/step (2.8x). With the subcycling driver and swap packing, MFC is 13% faster than PeleC here. Tile clustering is not shown: it currently runs out of memory with subcycling (store slots sized for full blocks; post-meeting fix).
AMR-only cost (each code's own RHS excluded), newest MFC build: 0.155 s/step subcycled at 128 GPUs vs AMReX 0.421 and PeleC 0.358; lock-step 0.048 vs AMReX 0.149.
Lock-step, newest MFC build: 0.243 s/step at 128 GPUs vs AMReX 0.224, efficiency 0.95 vs 0.76; previous build 0.89 vs 0.68 at 512.
Time to solution at 128 GPUs, newest MFC build: 149 s vs PeleC 172 s (13% faster) with WENO5 and more refined volume.
Subcycling order of accuracy: quartic prolongation (with regrid and two levels) is second order; minmod is first order.
Coarse-fine interface error relative to the uniform fine grid: quartic matches it; minmod is 10^4-10^5x worse.
Refined share of the domain: MFC refines ~1.3x more volume than AMReX/PeleC by default; tile clustering matches them but is not yet usable with subcycling (memory).
Same numerics, different programming model: Fortran OpenMP with the right loop structure is within ~12% of HIP; MFC's RHS cost is code structure, not OpenMP.
